newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Absa climbs as profits beat expectations.
newsitem.headline: Absa climbs as profits beat expectations.

text.p: Better-than-expected first half earnings from Absa pushed shares higher in early morning trade and dealers expected it to trade higher on the day.
Amalgamated Banks of South Africa Ltd (Absa) added 45 cents to its market value from an opening price of 23.30 shortly after interim results were announced at 0730 GMT.
Shares than dropped to 23.40 rand, 30 cents or 1.3 percent higher by 0748 GMT with a trded volume of 32,500 shares.

"Basically people are punting on the results which came out better than hoped for. It will carry on climbing on that but might shed a few gains as the market starts to settle. It's still early in trade," one dealer said.
Absa raised its interim share for the six months ended September 30 to 101 cents from 73.1 cents -- beating analysts expectations which ranged earnings per share between 91.4 cents and 96.5 cents.
The bank declared a dividend of 27 cents per share from 21.5 cents and offered a capitalisation share award.

But Absa also warned that earnings growth would slow in the second half of the year because credit demand was tapering off while the high money market shortage was likely to continue, exerting pressure on margins.
